page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is an x86_64 architecture server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it integrates three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in several areas. The AMD EPYC CPU achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside strong multi-core capabilities. Memory performance is robust, with top-tier large-block write bandwidth and strong read bandwidth. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency, processing prompts and generating text at high speeds for both 135M and 7B parameter models. However, software compilation and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the average tier.

The server offers high resource density for GPU-accelerated workloads, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for deep learning, LLM inference, and data-intensive processing. A key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions. This configuration is highly suited for machine learning inference, image processing, text processing, and high-throughput memory-bound computations.
